analyst_view.overall: Galatasaray are 18th of 36 with 6 points and Aston Villa 6th with 9, so both have plenty at stake: Okan Buruk's side want to climb into the top 24 at home, Villa want a top-8 place. Buruk confirmed on Monday that Victor Osimhen will not play (still in treatment, aimed at the Beşiktaş derby) and that Roland Sallai is also out; Rafael Leão is out too, and the numbers now count all three on goals. Ismail Jakobs is the only doubt, and UEFA expects Barış Alper Yılmaz to lead the line with Sané, Batrakov and Yunus Akgün behind him, so Galatasaray have no recognised centre-forward. Villa drew 0-0 with Sunderland; Matty Cash (concussion), Matteo Ruggeri and Amadou Onana are out and counted, Victor Lindelöf is expected to start after illness, and Emery says Villa are not favourites. German referee Daniel Siebert is in charge, and the RAMS Park pitch has needed repairs, so Villa were not allowed to train on it.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (1.1 Galatasaray, 1.8 Villa) and now take off Osimhen (-10%), Sallai and Leão (-5% each) from Galatasaray's goals, plus Cash for Villa. That covers what made me trim this morning, and the striker-less plan is just the other side of Osimhen's absence, so I drop my -6% and stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already counting Galatasaray's slight rise in corners won (+2.8%) and Villa's dip (-3.4%). Villa keep the ball and push wide with Maatsen and Wan-Bissaka, while Galatasaray lose width without Leão and Sallai but still have Sané and Yunus Akgün on the flanks; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with Galatasaray's quieter recent card count (-8.5%), Villa's slight rise (+3.6%) and Daniel Siebert's average record (4.1 a game, +1%) already in. RAMS Park is loud and hostile and both sides need points, but that is what a normal Champions League night here looks like, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots (12.8 Galatasaray, 13.7 Villa); they take the missing forwards off goals but not off shots. With Osimhen, Sallai and Leão all confirmed out and Barış Alper Yılmaz expected up front instead of a centre-forward, Galatasaray lose their main shot-takers, and a repaired pitch may slow the game; I trim to about 25.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, already counting Villa's sharper recent finishing (+5.9%) and Galatasaray's slight dip (-0.8%), but not the forwards Galatasaray are missing. Osimhen is the player who turns their chances into efforts on target, and Buruk confirmed he is out, so I keep my lean lower, to about 9.7.
